$readme: Figures this project has published and then RETRACTED, with the corrected value.
WHY: over three review rounds of PR #848 the same defect reproduced four times — a figure
corrected in one place while other copies kept publishing the old value. Round 3 found it had
reproduced outside the repo entirely, on the GitHub issues the release documents tell readers
carry the corrected findings. A per-instance fix is the wrong shape for a defect that recurs;
this ledger plus scripts/verify-retracted-figures.mjs is the gate.
HOW IT IS CHECKED: the verifier scans the cited documents for issue references (never an
enumerated list), fetches each issue's body and comments, and FAILS if any retracted figure
still stands with no correcting comment on that issue. A source that quotes a retracted figure
AND states its corrected value is a correction, and discharges that figure for the issue.
THE RESIDUAL, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: this ledger is written by whoever makes a retraction.
A retraction whose author never adds an entry here is not caught, and no scan can catch it,
because nothing in the tree marks the old value as wrong. That is a real limit of this gate,
not an oversight. What it does guarantee is that a figure recorded here cannot go on being
published uncorrected on a cited issue.
PATTERNS are matched after normalisation: markdown emphasis stripped, whitespace collapsed,
lowercased. Write the claim as prose; do not write a regex. Several surface forms per figure
are expected, because one claim gets written several ways.
PATTERNS MUST BE SPECIFIC TO THE WRONG CLAIM. '28 of 28' alone is CORRECT ('failed: 0 on 28 of
28') — only the conjunction with 778/0/0 is wrong. A pattern that matches the true statement
makes the gate unpassable and it will be deleted rather than fixed.
correctionSignature: the short phrase that must appear ALONGSIDE a quoted retracted
pattern for a source to count as correcting it. Quoting alone is republishing the
error; asserting the right value alone does not reach a reader who landed on the
comment carrying the wrong one. Both halves are required, which is what makes the
rule impossible to satisfy by relabelling a comment.

figures.wrong: The zero-re-runs figure is asserted twice, independently — the ledger's runAttempt and the API's run_attempt.
figures.correct: One GitHub counter read two ways. test-e2e-deploy.yml sets RUN_ATTEMPT from github.run_attempt and compat-run-ledger.mjs writes it through, so the ledger reading is not independent and is strictly weaker. The API reading is authoritative: run_attempt is 1 on all 72 scheduled runs, none above 1.

$why: Sentences that are TRUE and legitimate, and which no pattern above may match.
The $readme rule says patterns must be specific to the WRONG claim, but nothing enforced it,
so round-5 review found two entries breaking it: bare "asserted twice" flagged "the flag is
asserted twice in the reconciler for idempotency", and bare "9 restarts" flagged "the bun lane
saw 9 restarts in its own 27 nights" — the exact node-vs-bun vocabulary adjacency that is the
documented reason the general fuzzy check was NOT built.
The consequence is the one the ledger warns about: a TRUE statement on a cited issue reds the
gate with no legitimate remedy, and the cheapest path back to green becomes editing the ledger.
tests/retracted-figures.test.ts asserts every sentence here stays unmatched, so a future entry
sentences: The flag is asserted twice in the reconciler for idempotency.

failed: 0 on 28 of 28 ledgered nights, which is the correct statement.
The node lane ran 28 fingerprinted nights across two windows in an unrelated analysis.
